# Flow assurance

## `calculate_corrosion_rate`

Internal CO2/H2S corrosion rate over three models (de Waard-Lotz, sour with the Mariaca regime factor, NORSOK M-506), with NACE MR0175 region, inhibited rate and wall allowance.

**Price:** Costs 2 credits.

**In each client:** [Python](../python.md#graphsolve.GraphSolve.calculate_corrosion_rate) · [TypeScript](../typescript/api/classes/GraphSolve.md#calculate_corrosion_rate) · [Rust](https://docs.rs/graphsolve/latest/graphsolve/struct.GraphSolve.html#method.calculate_corrosion_rate)

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bicarbonate_molar` | number | no | Bicarbonate concentration [mol/L] — NORSOK in-situ pH |
| `co2_mole_fraction` | number | no | CO2 mole fraction in the gas phase |
| `design_life_years` | number | no | Design life [years], to report a wall-thickness allowance |
| `diameter` | number | no | Internal diameter [m] — NORSOK shear |
| `glycol_wt_pct` | number | no | Glycol concentration [wt %] — NORSOK mitigation |
| `h2s_mole_fraction` | number | no | H2S mole fraction in the gas phase |
| `inhibitor_efficiency_pct` | number | no | Corrosion-inhibitor efficiency [%] |
| `ionic_strength_molar` | number | no | Ionic strength [mol/L] — NORSOK in-situ pH |
| `mixture_density` | number | no | Mixture density [kg/m3] — NORSOK shear |
| `mixture_velocity` | number | no | Mixture velocity [m/s] — NORSOK shear |
| `mixture_viscosity` | number | no | Mixture viscosity [Pa.s] — NORSOK shear |
| `model` | string | no | Corrosion rate model (default de_waard_lotz) |
| `ph` | number | no | In-situ pH — NORSOK. Computed from the carbonate equilibrium when omitted. |
| `pressure` | number | yes | Local total pressure in MPa |
| `roughness` | number | no | Absolute roughness [m] — NORSOK shear (default 4.5e-5) |
| `shear_stress_pa` | number | no | Wall shear stress [Pa] — NORSOK. Computed from the flow state below when omitted. |
| `temperature` | number | yes | Local temperature in K |

### Example: NORSOK M-506 from the flow state

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from graphsolve import GraphSolve

    gs = GraphSolve()
    response = gs.calculate_corrosion_rate(
        bicarbonate_molar=0.002,
        co2_mole_fraction=0.03,
        diameter=0.25,
        glycol_wt_pct=30.0,
        ionic_strength_molar=0.5,
        mixture_density=180.0,
        mixture_velocity=6.0,
        mixture_viscosity=2e-05,
        model="norsok_m506",
        pressure=6.0,
        temperature=333.0,
    )
    print(response["result"])
    ```

=== "TypeScript"

    ```ts
    import { GraphSolve } from "@graphsolve/sdk";

    const gs = new GraphSolve();
    const response = await gs.calculate_corrosion_rate({
        "bicarbonate_molar": 0.002,
        "co2_mole_fraction": 0.03,
        "diameter": 0.25,
        "glycol_wt_pct": 30.0,
        "ionic_strength_molar": 0.5,
        "mixture_density": 180.0,
        "mixture_velocity": 6.0,
        "mixture_viscosity": 2e-05,
        "model": "norsok_m506",
        "pressure": 6.0,
        "temperature": 333.0
    });
    console.log(response.result);
    ```

=== "Rust"

    ```rust

    use serde_json::json;

    let gs = GraphSolve::new()?;
    let response = gs
        .call("calculate_corrosion_rate", &json!({
            "bicarbonate_molar": 0.002,
            "co2_mole_fraction": 0.03,
            "diameter": 0.25,
            "glycol_wt_pct": 30.0,
            "ionic_strength_molar": 0.5,
            "mixture_density": 180.0,
            "mixture_velocity": 6.0,

            "model": "norsok_m506",
            "pressure": 6.0,
            "temperature": 333.0
        }))
        .await?;

    ```

## `calculate_wax_deposition_rate`

Wax deposition rate on a cold wall from the subcooling and the wax solubility gradient — thickness in mm/yr and mass flux in g/m2/day.

**Price:** Costs 2 credits.

**In each client:** [Python](../python.md#graphsolve.GraphSolve.calculate_wax_deposition_rate) · [TypeScript](../typescript/api/classes/GraphSolve.md#calculate_wax_deposition_rate) · [Rust](https://docs.rs/graphsolve/latest/graphsolve/struct.GraphSolve.html#method.calculate_wax_deposition_rate)

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ambient_temperature` | number | yes | Ambient (outside-wall) temperature in K |
| `bulk_temperature` | number | yes | Bulk fluid temperature in K |
| `heat_transfer_coefficient` | number | yes | Overall heat-transfer coefficient [W/m2/K] |
| `oil_density` | number | yes | Oil density [kg/m3] |
| `oil_molecular_weight` | number | no | Oil molecular weight [g/mol] — for the Wilke-Chang diffusivity estimate |
| `oil_thermal_conductivity` | number | no | Oil thermal conductivity [W/m/K] |
| `oil_viscosity` | number | no | Oil viscosity [Pa.s] — for the Wilke-Chang diffusivity estimate |
| `solubility_gradient_per_k` | number | yes | Wax solubility gradient dWs/dT [1/K]: the slope of dissolved wax mass fraction against temperature. screen_wax_risk returns it for model sle. |
| `wax_diffusivity` | number | no | Wax diffusivity [m2/s]. Estimated by Wilke-Chang when omitted and the oil properties below are given. |
| `wax_molecular_weight` | number | no | Wax molecular weight [g/mol] — for the Wilke-Chang diffusivity estimate |

### Example: subsea line, Wilke-Chang diffusivity

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from graphsolve import GraphSolve

    gs = GraphSolve()
    response = gs.calculate_wax_deposition_rate(
        ambient_temperature=277.0,
        bulk_temperature=313.0,
        heat_transfer_coefficient=20.0,
        oil_density=850.0,
        oil_molecular_weight=200.0,
        oil_thermal_conductivity=0.13,
        oil_viscosity=0.005,
        solubility_gradient_per_k=0.0025,
        wax_molecular_weight=340.0,
    )
    print(response["result"])
    ```

    ```ts
        "oil_molecular_weight": 200.0,
        "oil_thermal_conductivity": 0.13,
        "oil_viscosity": 0.005,
    ```

## `evaluate_flow_assurance_profile`

Hydrate, corrosion and erosion screening along a whole line, each reporting the controlling sample — index, length, pressure and temperature — not just a worst-case number.

**Price:** Costs 8 credits, plus 1 per 250 ms beyond the first 4 s of compute.

**In each client:** [Python](../python.md#graphsolve.GraphSolve.evaluate_flow_assurance_profile) · [TypeScript](../typescript/api/classes/GraphSolve.md#evaluate_flow_assurance_profile) · [Rust](https://docs.rs/graphsolve/latest/graphsolve/struct.GraphSolve.html#method.evaluate_flow_assurance_profile)

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `c_factor` | number | no | API RP 14E C-factor for the erosion pass (default 100), in the standard's customary units (ft/s)(lb/ft3)^0.5. By service class: 100 continuous service in carbon steel, 125 intermittent service, 150 solids-free inhibited or corrosion-resistant-alloy service; 30 to 50 for sand-bearing production. |
| `component_names` | array | no | Component names, for the hydrate and corrosion passes |
| `heat_capacity` | number | no | Mixture heat capacity [J/kg/K] |
| `inhibitor_depression_k` | number | no | Hydrate inhibitor depression already applied to the line [K] |
| `inlet_mixture_density` | number | no | Inlet mixture density [kg/m3], for the erosion pass |
| `inlet_pressure` | number | yes | Inlet pressure [MPa] from the converged solve |
| `inlet_temperature` | number | yes | Inlet temperature [K] |
| `mass_flow` | number | yes | Total mass flow [kg/s] |
| `outlet_pressure` | number | yes | Outlet pressure [MPa] |
| `outlet_temperature` | number | yes | Outlet temperature [K] |
| `segments` | array of object | yes | Pipe geometry, inlet to outlet |
| `vapor_mole_fractions` | array | no | Inlet vapour mole fractions, aligned with component_names |

### Example: 5 km subsea tieback, sour gas

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from graphsolve import GraphSolve

    gs = GraphSolve()
    response = gs.evaluate_flow_assurance_profile(
        c_factor=100.0,
        component_names=["methane", "ethane", "propane", "CO2", "H2S"],
        inlet_mixture_density=95.0,
        inlet_pressure=9.0,
        inlet_temperature=333.0,
        mass_flow=22.0,
        outlet_pressure=6.5,
        outlet_temperature=283.0,
        segments=[
            {
                "angle": 90.0,
                "diameter": 0.25,
                "heat_transfer_coefficient": 20.0,
                "length": 3000.0,
                "surrounding_temperature": 277.0
            },
            {
                "angle": 75.0,
                "diameter": 0.25,
                "heat_transfer_coefficient": 18.0,
                "length": 2000.0,
                "surrounding_temperature": 277.0
            }
        ],
        vapor_mole_fractions=[0.86, 0.06, 0.03, 0.04, 0.01],
    )
    print(response["result"])
    ```

## `list_flow_assurance_models`

The model vocabularies the flow-assurance tools accept — hydrate, wax, asphaltene, corrosion and scale models with their tier, plus how wax formers are identified, inhibitor names, vdWP guests, the scale risk bands, the NACE MR0175 regions and the API RP 14E service classes.

**Price:** Free.

**In each client:** [Python](../python.md#graphsolve.GraphSolve.list_flow_assurance_models) · [TypeScript](../typescript/api/classes/GraphSolve.md#list_flow_assurance_models) · [Rust](https://docs.rs/graphsolve/latest/graphsolve/struct.GraphSolve.html#method.list_flow_assurance_models)

## `partition_acid_gas_in_water`

How much CO2 and H2S is dissolved in the produced water, and the in-situ pH that leaves — the brine pH the corrosion models should consume instead of a condensed-water estimate.

**Price:** Costs 2 credits.

**In each client:** [Python](../python.md#graphsolve.GraphSolve.partition_acid_gas_in_water) · [TypeScript](../typescript/api/classes/GraphSolve.md#partition_acid_gas_in_water) · [Rust](https://docs.rs/graphsolve/latest/graphsolve/struct.GraphSolve.html#method.partition_acid_gas_in_water)

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `co2_fugacity_bar` | number | no | CO2 fugacity [bar]. Supply this or co2_mole_fraction. The earlier name co2_fugacity is still accepted. |
| `co2_mass_rate` | number | no | Total CO2 mass rate in the stream [kg/s], to report the aqueous fraction |
| `co2_mole_fraction` | number | no | CO2 mole fraction in the gas phase, converted to a fugacity through the NORSOK fugacity coefficient at the given pressure and temperature. |
| `h2s_fugacity_bar` | number | no | H2S fugacity [bar]. Supply this or h2s_mole_fraction. The earlier name h2s_fugacity is still accepted. |
| `h2s_mass_rate` | number | no | Total H2S mass rate in the stream [kg/s], to report the aqueous fraction |
| `h2s_mole_fraction` | number | no | H2S mole fraction in the gas phase, converted to a partial pressure. |
| `ph` | number | no | Measured in-situ pH. Bypasses the charge-balance solve. |
| `pressure` | number | yes | Local total pressure in MPa |
| `temperature` | number | yes | Local temperature in K |
| `water_analysis` | object | yes | Produced-water ion analysis in mg/l |
| `water_mass_rate` | number | no | Produced-water mass rate [kg/s], to report the aqueous inventory as kg/day |

### Example: in-situ pH only, from a measured alkalinity

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from graphsolve import GraphSolve

    gs = GraphSolve()
    response = gs.partition_acid_gas_in_water(
        co2_fugacity_bar=1.5,
        pressure=5.0,
        temperature=320.0,
        water_analysis={
            "bicarbonate_mg_per_l": 1200.0,
            "chloride_mg_per_l": 17000.0,
            "sodium_mg_per_l": 12000.0
        },
    )
    print(response["result"])
    ```

=== "TypeScript"

    ```ts
    import { GraphSolve } from "@graphsolve/sdk";

    const gs = new GraphSolve();
    const response = await gs.partition_acid_gas_in_water({
        "co2_fugacity_bar": 1.5,
        "pressure": 5.0,
        "temperature": 320.0,
        "water_analysis": {
            "bicarbonate_mg_per_l": 1200.0,
            "chloride_mg_per_l": 17000.0,
            "sodium_mg_per_l": 12000.0
        }
    });
    console.log(response.result);
    ```

=== "Rust"

    ```rust
    use graphsolve::GraphSolve;
    use serde_json::json;

    let gs = GraphSolve::new()?;
    let response = gs
        .call("partition_acid_gas_in_water", &json!({
            "co2_fugacity_bar": 1.5,
            "pressure": 5.0,
            "temperature": 320.0,
            "water_analysis": {
                "bicarbonate_mg_per_l": 1200.0,
                "chloride_mg_per_l": 17000.0,
                "sodium_mg_per_l": 12000.0
            }
        }))
        .await?;
    println!("{:?}", response.result);
    ```

## `screen_hydrate_risk`

Hydrate formation temperature and margin at a live state, over four models (Towler-Mokhatab screening or vdW-Platteeuw sI / sII / combined), with Hammerschmidt inhibitor depression.

**Price:** Costs 2 credits.

**In each client:** [Python](../python.md#graphsolve.GraphSolve.screen_hydrate_risk) · [TypeScript](../typescript/api/classes/GraphSolve.md#screen_hydrate_risk) · [Rust](https://docs.rs/graphsolve/latest/graphsolve/struct.GraphSolve.html#method.screen_hydrate_risk)

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `component_names` | array | no | Component names. Required by the vdWP models — a specific gravity carries no cavity-occupancy information. |
| `inhibitor` | string | no | Thermodynamic inhibitor |
| `inhibitor_wt_pct` | number | no | Inhibitor mass fraction in the WATER phase [wt %], not in the bulk stream |
| `model` | string | no | Hydrate thermodynamics (default vdwp_combined) |
| `mole_fractions` | array | no | Vapour mole fractions, aligned with component_names |
| `molecular_weights` | array | no | Component molecular weights [g/mol], to derive a specific gravity for towler_mokhatab |
| `pressure` | number | yes | Local pressure in MPa |
| `specific_gravity` | number | no | Gas specific gravity (air = 1). towler_mokhatab only; derived from the composition when omitted. |
| `temperature` | number | yes | Local operating temperature in K |

### Example: screening correlation with 20 wt% MEG

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from graphsolve import GraphSolve

    gs = GraphSolve()
    response = gs.screen_hydrate_risk(
        inhibitor="meg",
        inhibitor_wt_pct=20.0,
        model="towler_mokhatab",
        pressure=10.0,
        specific_gravity=0.62,
        temperature=285.0,
    )
    print(response["result"])
    ```

=== "TypeScript"

    ```ts
    import { GraphSolve } from "@graphsolve/sdk";

    const gs = new GraphSolve();
    const response = await gs.screen_hydrate_risk({
        "inhibitor": "meg",
        "inhibitor_wt_pct": 20.0,
        "model": "towler_mokhatab",
        "pressure": 10.0,
        "specific_gravity": 0.62,
        "temperature": 285.0
    });
    console.log(response.result);
    ```

=== "Rust"

    ```rust
    use graphsolve::GraphSolve;
    use serde_json::json;

    let gs = GraphSolve::new()?;
    let response = gs
        .call("screen_hydrate_risk", &json!({
            "inhibitor": "meg",
    ```

## `screen_scale_risk`

Mineral-scale saturation indices from a produced-water ion analysis — calcite, aragonite, siderite, barite, celestite, gypsum, anhydrite and halite — with the precipitable mass and the limiting ion.

**Price:** Costs 2 credits.

**In each client:** [Python](../python.md#graphsolve.GraphSolve.screen_scale_risk) · [TypeScript](../typescript/api/classes/GraphSolve.md#screen_scale_risk) · [Rust](https://docs.rs/graphsolve/latest/graphsolve/struct.GraphSolve.html#method.screen_scale_risk)

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `co2_fugacity_bar` | number | no | CO2 fugacity [bar]. Supply this or co2_mole_fraction. The earlier name co2_fugacity is still accepted. |
| `co2_mole_fraction` | number | no | CO2 mole fraction in the gas phase, converted to a fugacity through the NORSOK fugacity coefficient at the given pressure and temperature. |
| `h2s_fugacity_bar` | number | no | H2S fugacity [bar]. Supply this or h2s_mole_fraction. The earlier name h2s_fugacity is still accepted. |
| `h2s_mole_fraction` | number | no | H2S mole fraction in the gas phase, converted to a partial pressure. |
| `minerals` | array | no | Restrict the screen to these minerals. Omit for all eight. |
| `ph` | number | no | Measured in-situ pH. Bypasses the charge-balance solve. |
| `pressure` | number | yes | Local total pressure in MPa |
| `temperature` | number | yes | Local temperature in K |
| `water_analysis` | object | yes | Produced-water ion analysis in mg/l |
| `water_mass_rate` | number | no | Produced-water mass rate [kg/s], to report scale as a mass rate |

### Example: calcite only, across a choke where CO2 breaks out

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from graphsolve import GraphSolve

    gs = GraphSolve()
    response = gs.screen_scale_risk(
        co2_fugacity_bar=1.0,
        minerals=["calcite", "aragonite"],
        pressure=2.0,
        temperature=325.0,
        water_analysis={
            "bicarbonate_mg_per_l": 600.0,
            "calcium_mg_per_l": 2500.0,
            "chloride_mg_per_l": 50000.0,
            "sample_density_kg_per_m3": 1055.0,
            "sodium_mg_per_l": 30000.0
        },
    )
    print(response["result"])
    ```

    ```ts
            "bicarbonate_mg_per_l": 600.0,
            "calcium_mg_per_l": 2500.0,

            "sample_density_kg_per_m3": 1055.0,
            "sodium_mg_per_l": 30000.0
    ```

## `screen_wax_risk`

Wax appearance temperature and margin over three tiers: a C7+ screening correlation, the Won multi-solid SLE, or the non-ideal SLE flash with per-component solid fractions, measured melting data and the solubility gradient for the deposition rate.

**Price:** Costs 2 credits.

**In each client:** [Python](../python.md#graphsolve.GraphSolve.screen_wax_risk) · [TypeScript](../typescript/api/classes/GraphSolve.md#screen_wax_risk) · [Rust](https://docs.rs/graphsolve/latest/graphsolve/struct.GraphSolve.html#method.screen_wax_risk)

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `activity_model` | string | no | Activity model - sle model (default regular_solution) |
| `component_names` | array | no | Component names, aligned with mole_fractions - won and sle models. When wax_former_mask is omitted, a name that resolves to a normal paraffin (n-hexadecane, n-C24, ...) is a wax former if it is n-C16 or heavier; any other name falls back to the molecular-weight threshold. The sle result also names its dominant wax former from this list. |
| `density_c7_plus` | number | no | C7+ density [kg/m3] - screening model |
| `enthalpies_of_fusion` | array | no | Measured enthalpies of fusion [J/mol] per component - won and sle models. Nulls fall back to the Won correlation. |
| `enthalpies_of_transition` | array | no | Solid-solid transition enthalpies [J/mol] per component - sle model |
| `heat_capacity_correction` | boolean | no | Apply the heat-capacity-of-fusion correction - sle model (default true). Uses heat_capacity_of_fusion_j_per_mol_k where given, else the Pedersen correlation. |
| `heat_capacity_of_fusion_j_per_mol_k` | array | no | Heat capacity of fusion, Cp(liquid) - Cp(solid) [J/(mol K)], per component - sle model, applied when heat_capacity_correction is on. Nulls fall back to the Pedersen correlation. |
| `liquid_molar_volume_cm3_per_mol` | array | no | Liquid molar volumes [cm3/mol] per component - sle model activity coefficients. Nulls fall back to the Won paraffin-density correlation, or a light-hydrocarbon fit below 70 g/mol. |
| `liquid_solubility_parameter_mpa_half` | array | no | Liquid solubility parameters [MPa^0.5] per component - sle model activity coefficients. Nulls fall back to a correlation in molar mass. |
| `melting_points` | array | no | Measured melting points [K] per component - won and sle models. Nulls fall back to the Won correlation. |
| `model` | string | no | Wax model (default screening) |
| `mole_fractions` | array | no | Component mole fractions - won and sle models |
| `molecular_weights` | array | no | Component molecular weights [g/mol] - won and sle models |
| `mw_c7_plus` | number | no | C7+ molecular weight [g/mol] - screening model |
| `paraffin_mass_fraction` | number | no | Paraffin mass fraction of the C7+ cut - screening model |
| `solid_molar_volume_ratio` | number | no | Solid-to-liquid molar volume ratio - sle model (default 1: the solid and liquid molar volumes are taken as equal). Must be positive. |
| `temperature` | number | yes | Local operating temperature in K |
| `transition_temperatures` | array | no | Solid-solid (rotator-phase) transition temperatures [K] per component - sle model |
| `watson_k` | number | no | Watson K, used to estimate the paraffin fraction when it is not supplied - screening model |
| `wax_former_mask` | array | no | Which components are wax formers - won and sle models. Omit to identify them from component_names, or without names from a molecular-weight threshold of about n-C16 (226.45 g/mol). |

### Example: C7+ screening

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from graphsolve import GraphSolve

    gs = GraphSolve()
    response = gs.screen_wax_risk(
        density_c7_plus=840.0,
        model="screening",
        mw_c7_plus=220.0,
        paraffin_mass_fraction=0.35,
        temperature=300.0,
    )
    print(response["result"])
    ```

=== "TypeScript"

    ```ts

    const gs = new GraphSolve();
    const response = await gs.screen_wax_risk({
        "density_c7_plus": 840.0,
        "model": "screening",
        "mw_c7_plus": 220.0,
        "paraffin_mass_fraction": 0.35,
        "temperature": 300.0
    });
    console.log(response.result);
    ```

=== "Rust"

    ```rust
        }))
    ```
